description: This plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics: Final Accuracy, $\Delta$ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" and features a linear scale ranging from approximately 0.82 to 0.99, with tick marks spaced at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and uses a linear scale with visible tick marks ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 at intervals of 0.2, though the plotted data extends above this labeled range. The "Final Accuracy" is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers and error bars; it begins at an initial confidence of 0.82 with an accuracy value near 1.0, experiences a slight dip at 0.83 to roughly 0.95, and then exhibits a general upward trend, concluding at an initial confidence of 0.99 with an accuracy value of approximately 1.25. The "Initial Accuracy" is depicted by a dash-dot green line with square markers and error bars, starting at 0.82 with a value of approximately 0.55, showing an overall upward trajectory with minor dips at 0.86 (value near 0.8) and 0.90 (value near 0.95), and ending at 0.99 with a value of roughly 1.2. Finally, the "$\Delta$ Accuracy" is shown as a dashed orange line with diamond markers and error bars; it begins at 0.82 with a value of approximately 0.45, fluctuates across the x-axis reaching a low point of roughly 0.3 at 0.86 and a peak of approximately 0.7 at 0.93, before ending at 0.99 with a value near 0.6.
